txt: It doesn't look like he knows what that means.
Just a second ago, the first one was laughing. Now he's doing something with his lip and his gap tooth.
One of the boys nods, the other one looks at his brother and shrugs.
The boy draws a jagged rock across the ground. It leaves a white scratch.
The boy keeps laughing. Then he bows down to inspect the rock as though there's something noteworthy about it.
The boy stops laughing and looks at his toes.
The kids don't reply, absorbed in their little game.
The other boy straightens his back. "I'm not gonna start *crying*, stupid," he snaps, regaining control of his quivering chin.
The scruffy-haired little boy kicks a stone while the other watches him do it.
The scruffy-haired little boy kicks a stone. He can't be more than five years old.
The stone-kicker laughs suddenly. His head is too large for his shoulders.
The stone-kicking one becomes frantic all of a sudden, as if that's something to be scared of -- the obvious fact that you just stated.
This one doesn't say anything, kicking the concrete with his worn-out sneaker.
"'It is time at last, my nasty speedfreaks! Our brotherman is about to grow up!'"
"'Turn up the volume, blow those speakers out. Now here's---'"
"Because.... because..." The boy pauses to think.
"Don't say more bad words!" The boy frowns.
"Ha ha, I dunno what you're talking about." One of the boys shrugs his shoulders and starts laughing.
"Ha-ha," the scruffy-haired little kid laughs, as though in agreement.
"He dunno what you're talking about," the first kid says loudly. Or you think it's the first kid -- it could be the second.
"Huh..." The first one pauses to think, then comes to some kind of conclusion. "He doesn't live there. He isn't there sometimes."
"I don't know what those are..."
"I don't know," they say almost in unison.
"I don't know..." The boy who made the claim finds himself unsure of it. He looks around.
"I dunno what you're talking about." The boy stuffs his hands deep into his pockets and kicks another rock.
"I'm not gonna start *crying*," the one who almost started crying snaps, regaining control of his quivering chin.
"I'm sorry." The one says to the other, rubbing his brother's shoulder affectionately.
"I..." starts one of them -- it's hard to tell which one now. "I don't know."
"Maybe *you're* stupid!"
"Mhm," his brother nods. "Gather the sticks for the fire -- and bullets. Or not real bullets, empty bullets."
"Mhm. Lily's our mom," says one of the twins.
"No, he doesn't live there. I don't think."
"No," the boy answers, shaking his head vehemently.
"Oh..." The boy looks uncomfortable, at the jetty toward his mother.
"Okay." The scruffy-haired boy squints up at you.
"On that island?" The one who's busy kicking his stone points to the bay.
"Our father killed himself."
"Please don't..." The boy's eyes well up as he looks at you. They're dark and round. The wind tussles his hair.
"Radio? What's that?" The boy sniffs up a drip of snot. "We just heard them. In our head."
"That's... uhm... nothing?" The boy pauses to think with his finger in his mouth. "It's just a seafort and some plants. You can take a raft there. It's great."
"There are lights. The fire guy comes and asks us to put the fire out."
"There's a..." the boy says, rubbing his eyes. It's clear that he has no intention of finishing the sentence.
"There." The boy points toward one of the ruined monoliths nearby.
"Uh-huh!" one says, throwing a rock into the sand.
"Uh..." He scratches his head. He looks at his twin, who nods -- and then he begins. "It was like... 'It is time at last, my nasty speedfreaks! Our brotherman is about to grow up!'"
"Uhm... I don't know. He doesn't like it. He doesn't like people to be there. You shouldn't go."
"Uhm... yes." The boy looks at his toes.
"Uhm..." The boy turns a rock over in his hand. "We heard *bad* words and said them, and got in trouble..."
"We learned," the other replies.
"We thought the voices were funny." The brother nods. "We said what they said and then we got in trouble..."
"What bad people?" One of the twins looks up, his mouth slightly open.
"What's a Feld building?" one of the twins asks with a shrug.
"Yeah." The boy turns a rock over in his hand. "We heard *bad* words and said them, and got in trouble..."
"Yes."
"You're stupid," the other one repeats, still deathly serious.
